purpose: Automatically detect valid tokens from events/logs and safely merge them into an allowlist file in a deterministic, auditable manner.
capabilities: Extract candidate tokens from heterogeneous events (strings and dict payloads)
Validate tokens using a strict default regex or a custom validator
Idempotent behavior: only new tokens are added, no removals by default
Atomic file writes to prevent torn or partial files
Optional backups with deterministic timestamp formatting
Deterministic ordering of tokens for stable diffs and reviews

inputs.allowlist_path: Path to the allowlist file to read and update
inputs.events: Iterable of strings or objects from which a candidate token may be extracted
inputs.validator: Optional callable to accept/reject tokens (defaults to a conservative regex)
inputs.timestamp: UTC compact format YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ for backup filenames (optional)

AllowlistDiff.additions: Set of tokens that were added to the allowlist
AllowlistDiff.removals: Set of tokens that were removed (empty in recovery mode)

outputs.filesystem: Updated allowlist file; optional backup copy when enabled

flow: Load existing allowlist (if present) and parse into a token set, ignoring comments and blanks
Extract candidate tokens from events using common keys or direct string lines
Filter candidates through the token validator and drop existing entries
If there are changes and backups are enabled, create a backup copy with the provided or generated timestamp
Serialize the updated token set in canonical sorted order with a trailing newline
Atomically replace the target allowlist file

data_model.token: String without whitespace, matching the validation policy
data_model.file_format: Text file, one token per line; lines beginning with '#' are treated as comments

security_considerations: Default validator restricts tokens to a conservative character set and maximum length to mitigate injection or path traversal via token values
Backups are created via atomic writes to avoid race conditions and ensure integrity
No external network or environment access is performed; all operations are local and explicit
Deterministic serialization minimizes unpredictable side effects and simplifies audit/review

determinism.ordering: Tokens are always sorted lexicographically before writing
determinism.timestamps: Tests can supply explicit timestamps; otherwise a UTC timestamp is generated at runtime
determinism.idempotency: Repeated recovery with identical events results in no file changes

extensibility.custom_validator: Callers can inject domain-specific validation logic
extensibility.parsers: _extract_candidates can be extended to support additional event shapes
